# engineering/geometry

<!-- Generated by scripts/okf.py index. Do not edit by hand. -->

# Section

* [Garment geometry](about.md) - Geometry techniques for designing a leotard directly on the body and turning it into production pattern pieces: surface layer instead of cloth simulation, body models, curves and panels on surfaces, flattening with stretch compensation, surface addresses, stone distribution, collision checks, size transfer and library options.

# Technique

* [Body models](body-models.md) - Anny (Apache-2.0 on CC0 MakeHuman assets, continuous child-to-adult) is the only verified commercially usable all-ages parametric body; SMPL-family models are non-commercial with licensing in flux; the POC uses MakeHuman via MPFB; fixed topology is the keystone.
* [Curves on surfaces](curves-on-surfaces.md) - Store design lines as control points on the body surface (face + barycentric) and evaluate them as geodesic or subdivision splines (flip geodesics, b/Surf, Mancinelli et al.); evaluate once on the reference body and carry to other sizes by barycentrics.
* [Fabric bridging hollows](fabric-bridging-hollows.md) - Stretch fabric spans body concavities (sternum, under and between the bust, lower back, gluteal cleft, underarm, crotch) instead of following them; the POC models this with an outward-only membrane offset solved per body.
* [Garment as a layer on the body surface](garment-as-surface-layer.md) - A skin-tight leotard can live on the body surface, as in Montes et al. (SIGGRAPH 2020), so no cloth simulation is needed in the interactive loop; simulation is reserved for parts that leave the skin and for background fit read-outs.
* [Geometry libraries and porting cost](geometry-libraries.md) - The mature geometry-processing libraries (geometry-central MIT, libigl MPL-2.0, pmp-library MIT; CGAL GPL/commercial) are C++; no production-grade JS/WASM or Rust equivalent was verified, so the needed kernel must be compiled to WASM or hand-written.
* [Local parameterisation for stamps](local-parameterisation-for-stamps.md) - Place motifs, spirals and decals by defining them in the tangent plane at a centre point and pushing them to the surface with the exponential map; use a log map (Affine Heat Method, MMP) for the inverse; parameterise the region itself for large motifs.
* [Pattern flattening](pattern-flattening.md) - Flattening a leotard panel to a pattern piece is a solved, fast computation: cut to a disk, conformal initialisation (LSCM or BFF), isometric refinement (ARAP or SLIM), then stretch compensation, seam-length reconciliation, allowance offset and markings; keep a stable design atlas separate from the production atlas.
* [Regions and panels from curves](regions-and-panels-from-curves.md) - Turn typed design curves into colour regions and pattern panels by inserting them into a working copy of the body mesh and labelling the cells (explicit arrangement), with winding numbers or signed distance as fallbacks; cut-outs, straps and edges are region and line types.
* [Size and pose transfer](size-and-pose-transfer.md) - Carry a design across sizes and poses through the shared body topology: curves and anchors ride by barycentrics; stone groups offer keep-count (pitch scales with the body) or keep-spacing (count scales ~s or ~s^2) semantics, with a per-size report.
* [Stone distribution algorithms](stone-distribution-algorithms.md) - Every stone brush is a curve or region on the surface, a sampler (arc-length, hex or square lattice, Poisson disk, Fermat spiral, contour-parallel) and a collision pass; formulas, defaults and non-destructive generator design.
* [Stretch compensation](stretch-compensation.md) - Turning a zero-ease flattened panel into a production piece: level 1 anisotropic per-fabric scaling (industry-equivalent), level 2 flattening against a target stretch tensor, level 3 physics-based optimisation; plus the tension criterion, Laplace pressure and print pre-distortion.
* [Surface addressing and picking](surface-addressing.md) - Anchor every stone and curve point as canonical face id + barycentric coordinates (attribute interpolation, as in Houdini and Blender), with a stable-UV fallback address; pick the body by BVH or a face-id GPU pass, and stones by an ID buffer.
* [Two-state collision checks](two-state-collision-checks.md) - Stones are rigid but the fabric is not: a layout spaced on the stretched (worn) body sits 15-20% closer on the relaxed pattern piece, so overlap and spacing checks must run in both states, mapped through the per-panel stretch factors.
